previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a complex history including acute myeloid leukemia in remission, stem cell transplant status, systolic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, chronic kidney disease stage 5, and recent C. difficile colitis, was admitted with acute decompensated heart failure following a brief stay at home after rehabilitation. He presented with sudden-onset chest pain and severe shortness of breath. Evaluation revealed elevated heart pressures, bilateral pleural effusions, and worsening renal function. He underwent right heart catheterization with endomyocardial biopsy, which showed reduced cardiac output and no evidence of graft-versus-host disease in the heart. He was treated in the CCU with IV diuresis, afterload reduction with hydralazine and isosorbide mononitrate, and continued oral vancomycin for active C. diff colitis. His symptoms improved, renal function stabilized, and he was transitioned to oral torsemide. He was discharged home with services, including home physical therapy and outpatient follow-up, with instructions to monitor weight, continue medications, and complete his antibiotic course.
